posts.headline: Patch now: Microsoft's July 2026 Windows Update closes 127 security holes
posts.tip: Open Settings > Windows Update and click Check for updates, then install the July 2026 cumulative update - it patches 127 flaws including a wormable remote-code-execution bug.
posts.truth: Most people think 'if it ain't broke, don't update.' That thinking is what gets folks crypto-locked. The bad actors are already writing exploits the day Microsoft publishes these holes.

posts.headline: Stop paying for Microsoft Office - LibreOffice is free and opens every Word, Excel and PowerPoint file
posts.tip: Download LibreOffice free from libreoffice.org - it opens, edits and saves .docx, .xlsx and .pptx with no Microsoft 365 subscription.
posts.truth: I see people paying $100 a year just to open a resume or a tax form. You don't need a subscription to read your own documents.

posts.headline: Your games and apps stutter - update your NVIDIA GeForce driver free
posts.tip: Download the latest GeForce driver free from nvidia.com/geforce/drivers (or open NVIDIA GeForce Experience and hit Check for updates) - it stops crashes and closes driver security holes.
posts.truth: Half the 'my computer is slow' calls I get are just a two-year-old graphics driver. People blame the hardware and go shopping for a new PC when a 5-minute download would've fixed it.

posts.headline: Your drive can fail with no warning - CrystalDiskInfo reads its health free
posts.tip: Install CrystalDiskInfo free from crystalmark.info, run it, and read the health status at the top - Caution or Bad means copy your files now before the drive gives out.
posts.truth: Drives don't get sick - they just die. The SMART data on the drive knows it's in trouble weeks before you see a blue screen, and Windows won't tell you.

posts.headline: Want private AI that never leaves your PC - Ollama runs it free
posts.tip: Install Ollama free from ollama.com, then run `ollama run llama3` in a terminal to chat with an AI model that never sends your data to the cloud.
posts.truth: Every cloud AI you use is reading what you type. For most folks that's fine. But the moment you paste a tax return or a customer list into one of those boxes, it's not your data anymore.

posts.headline: That computer you just bought came loaded with junk — here's how to clear it
posts.tip: Open Settings > Apps > Installed apps and uninstall the trialware and 'Get started' cruft; for a safe full sweep I run a debloat script that strips the rest without touching the operating system.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize a brand-new machine is the slowest it'll ever be on day one. The manufacturer stuffs it with adware trials and "buy me" tiles to make a few extra dollars, and that's what drags your boot time down before you've even opened a browser.

posts.headline: Stop renting Office for $100/yr — LibreOffice is free and opens every file you have
posts.tip: Download LibreOffice (free, no subscription) and it opens, edits, and saves every Word, Excel, and PowerPoint file you already own.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize they're renting software they used to own outright. Microsoft 365 has crept up to around $100 a year and people just keep paying because they think there's no other way. There is.

posts.headline: Six Zero-Days Live: Patch These Now
posts.tip: Six vulnerabilities are already under active attack today (July 13, 2026) — including flaws in Adobe ColdFusion, Langflow, and a cluster of Joomla extensions. No vendor patches exist yet for the new disclosures. If you run any of those tools, isolate them and watch for fixes. (Source: CVE Brief, July 13, 2026)
posts.truth: Today in tech: Apple sued OpenAI over alleged trade-secret theft by former Apple staff now building AI hardware; Google DeepMind's Gemini 3.5 Pro is targeted for a July 17 launch with a 2-million-token context window. (Sources: CNBC/NYT; Geeky-Gadgets)

posts.headline: Free AI Background Remover That Works in Seconds — Pixlr
posts.tip: Upload any photo to Pixlr's free AI background remover (pixlr.com/remove-background) — it cuts out backgrounds in seconds, no signup required, and works great for product photos or profile pics.
posts.truth: Most people don't realize you don't need Photoshop or a subscription for clean cutouts anymore. I see folks paying $20/month for Adobe just to remove backgrounds when free tools do it better and faster.

posts.headline: Stop Using SMS for 2FA — Use Bitwarden Auth or Aegis
posts.tip: Switch your important accounts (email, banking, social) to an authenticator app like Bitwarden Auth or Aegis — install from your app store (or getaenis.io/auth), SMS codes can be intercepted via SIM swapping.
posts.truth: I see hacked accounts every week where someone's phone number got ported out. SMS 2FA is better than nothing, but it's the weakest link. An authenticator app on your phone takes 30 seconds to set up and stops SIM-swap attacks cold.

posts.headline: Your Browser Is Leaking Data — Fix It With uBlock Origin
posts.tip: Install uBlock Origin (ublock.org) or uBlock Origin Lite — it blocks trackers, ads, and fingerprinting scripts that follow you across sites. It's free, open-source, and works instantly.
posts.truth: Most people think "incognito mode" protects them. It doesn't — it only hides history from other users on your computer. Trackers still see everything. A proper blocker stops them at the network level.

posts.headline: Windows 11 24H2 Is Breaking These Things ⚠️
posts.tip: The 24H2 update breaks some older drivers (especially audio and Wi-Fi), removes WordPad, and can reset default apps. Check your sound and network after updating — roll back drivers if needed.
posts.truth: Microsoft pushes updates like they're perfect. They're not. I've had three laptops this month come in with no sound or Wi-Fi after 24H2. A 5-minute driver rollback fixes it, but most people think their hardware died.
